High-Level Requirement:
  Summary: W3C Web Authentication - Two Factor (preview)
  Description: Epic brief: 
Summary: Add support to use FIDO2 and FIDO U2F security keys for two factor authentication
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Reset Credentials Flow does not delete existing OTP
  Description: With a default installation of the latest keycloak version also any previous version with flow contains a conditional action to when the user has 2FA enabled.
That means when the user chooses he will first need to reconfigure the OTP and after that choose a new password.
During the action, the existing authenticator should be deleted. This is not what is happening currently. Instead the existing authenticator is kept and an additional authenticator is created.
The user is not aware of this and will generally choose the same name for the authenticator as he used before. Thus he will be unable to differentiate between the old and new authenticators. I.e. after resetting his password the user will have a hard time logging in.
Even if the user was so lucky as to use a new name for the authenticator, he will be confused by having to select which authenticator to use, when one is obsolete.
This issue is somewhat related to KEYCLOAK-13134.

  Summary: Refactor login screens to not show many credentials of same type in credential selector
  Description: We discussed refactoring of login screens in a way, that credential selector won't show multiple credentials of same type. 
For example assume that user can choose between 3 alternatives when configuring authentication flow: password, OTP and WebAuthn. And assume that particular user john has 1 password, 2 OTP credentials and 2 WebAuthn credentials. Flow is configured as on slide 5 here: . So what will happen is:
- After providing username, user will see the screen with "Password" as that is his preferred credential. No credential selector would be displayed.
- User can click to link "Try another way"
- When he clicks on it, he will be able to choose between "Password", "Authenticator App" (which is OTP) and "Security Key" (which is WebAuthn). The page for OTP will show him available OTP credentials etc.
See slides 4-15 here for more details: .

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: After password reset, the new password has low priority
  Description: Reported by [~tkyjovsk@redhat.com] in KEYCLOAK-11922: after every password update the order of the credential items changes. The newly set password is at the very bottom of the table. Not sure if this is a bug.
Reply by [~mposolda@redhat.com]: yes, the fact that newly updated password is at the very bottom of the table is a bug IMO.
The first credential in the table is "preferred credential" . So for example assume that user has 1 password credential and 1 OTP credential in the table and password is at the top. Then if after updating the password, the password is at the bottom, it means that password is now not preferred credential, but instead the OTP credential is preferred. This could have some side-effects for some authentication flows configurations. The password should ideally remain in same place as it was before.
Will be also good to ensure the same behaviour (password at the same place) is during reset by admin and also when reset by user himself through the account console.

- Not sender-constraint. This is because "OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens Enabled" was OFF.
- Signed with RS256. This is because "Access Token Signature Algorithm" and "ID Token Signature Algorithm" were not specified.
- "redirect_uri" is not checked. This is because "Valid Redirect URIs" was "*".
I think it's good that we are not forced to change the client settings to be suitable for each security profile.
This is because one of the client policy's purposes is avoiding the over 40 settings for those security profiles.
It's OK if the client acts suitable for the selected security profile no matter what the client settings are.
But it's NG if the client acts not suitable for the selected security profile (like the above) with no error.

  Summary: Specify Signature Algorithm in Signed JWT Client Authentication
  Description: The current keycloak verifies the signed JWT by using the signature algorithm that this signed JWT's JOSE header's "alg" field tells.
This seems to be not secure because the client can use the algorithm that is considered to be not secure(e.g. RS256) and the keycloak accepts it.
Therefore, the allowed signature algorithm for Signed JWT client authentication can be set in advance expilcitly according to the client metadata "token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg" defined by OIDC Client Dynamic Registration (
Keycloak refuses the signed JWT that is signed by using the signature algorithm other than this registered signature algorithm.
For backward compatibility, if this allowed signature algorithm is not set, keycloak works as it is.

The problem is that the {{other/*}} test modules depend on the {{base}} module for common classes and test-classes while the {{base}} module also contains its own tests. This means it needs to be built twice: once with {{-DskipTests}} before the other modules can run, and once to run it's own tests.
Solution would be to move the common classes (arq. extensions, page objects, utils, etc) and the *abstract* test classes to a separate "framework" module and remove dependency of the other modules on the {{base}} module:
{noformat}
- testsuite:
 - integration-arquillian:
 - framework
 - servers: ...
 - tests:
  - base
  - adapters
  - admin-ui
  - mod-auth-mellon
  - ...
{noformat}

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Design proposal for login screen for select 2 factor authenticators
  Description: We may want some nice design for the login screens. The ideal candidate to start with could be the page for selecting alternative 2-factor authenticators.
The page might be similar to the slide 12 on those slides - . Few more additional points to clarify:
- This particular example uses password, OTP and WebAuthn as 2nd factor authenticators. In reality, password will likely never be 2nd factor authenticator, but for this example, we can assume that it may be and we may need the icon for it as well.
- The labels will be just "Password", "Authenticator application" and "Security key" . There 
won't be text like "Login with" at the beginning. These texts will be provided by authenticator implementations, no need to care too much about concrete texts in the design
- There will be some nice icon at the beginning for each authentication mechanism. Each authenticator will be able to provide CSS class of it's own.
- Ideal will be if there is arrow at the end of each line, so it is more clear that this is clickable link. Or something like this.
- Lines between items could be nice. Also some nice border for the table maybe...
- We may want to display username/email on this screen as well. As user (or at least his username) will be already known. Username can be displayed above the table. When user clicks on this username, the whole authentication flow should be restarted. It may be nice if it is somehow emphasized that username is clickable and that clicking on it will restart the login. Or alternatively, we can add hover like "Restart authentication" when user move his mouse over this username.
- We can inspire from Google regarding login screen. I am adding screenshot google-2factor.png for the inspiration. One thing, where we can be better than google could be the "username" link - we can make it more clear that click on it will restart the login.
- We can take a look at Patternfly components and possibly re-use some of them, so we don't need to create our own custom thing

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Cleanup ftl templates for all dynamic user profile related actions (register, update/verify profile, IDP review)
  Description: As part of the configurable User Profile, we are working on dynamic templates for auth flow actions (KEYCLOAK-18428, KEYCLOAK-18429) and we should consider one more general change. I think now is the good time to change/clear this area as we are going to introduce new dynamic templates when configurable user profile is enabled, so there is not major impact on backward compatibility (old realms with legacy user profile will use old templates still)
Current state is that there are two "static" templates for these actions:
* {{register.ftl}} for registration form
* {{login-update-profile.ftl}} used for 'update profile' required action and for 'IDP review' - by my experience, this one mixes together two things which are a bit different (IDP review is more like new account registration) and is a bit hard to customize as context is not clearly available in it.
Both templates are very similar, {{register.ftl}} has password and re-captcha sections on top of update. By my experience from template customization for sso.redhat.com, customizing template means to do a lots of duplicate work in these two templates, and customizing {{login-update-profile.ftl}} is not easy due to its duality and not clear context info.
So I can see three possible ways where to go:
1. use only one template for all these action, with clear CONTEXT info available from freemarker context, so no duplicate code but customization per action still possible - IMHO this is the best option
2. keep two templates as is, add clear CONTEXT info into dynamic version of the login-update-profile.ftl to make it's customization a bit easier (this one will be also used for 'Verify profile' action automatically forced by user profile rules checks) - close to current state, but IMHO not a very good solution for template customization
3. create separate template for each action - solves problem with login-update-profile.ftl duality, but IMHO adds lots of duplicate code and maintenance work.
We have to discuss this change in community first to collect experience from other template customizers.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Valid Redirect URI for review apps (wildcard in hostname?)
  Description: I'm using gitlab to handle code and it has this great feature called "review apps". This feature makes every feature branch deployed to a site so interested parties can review it before it is merged. So if you create a new branch called "my-cool-feature" it will automatically deploy to a site called "my-cool-feature.myapp.mycompany.com".
Now I wanted to use review apps with an application that is protected by keycloak. Everything worked great until I got to the Valid Redirect URI part. I previously did not understand that it only accepted a wildcard at the end. The origin URI accepts wildcards in the hostname so I found it natural that redirect uri would too. However after reading the documentation I found this section:
> Wildcards ( * ) are only allowed at the end of a URI, i.e. 
So my question is if there is any possibility to add a feature that allows for use with this kind of dynamic sites. I cannot really predict all the feature branch names that developers will create so they cannot really be pre-registered. If valid redirect URI would allow for something like that would solve it directly. I found some previous discussions about having a wildcard in the host part:
Of course there are the usual security concerns etc. I think having a wildcard in the host of valid redirect uri would be really useful for some development scenarios but should probably not be used in production. It would be nice if I as a server admin could make that decision though, instead of not having the option at all. Also I think with the cloud, container, and k8s environments we have today everything is more dynamic, sites are created and deleted on a daily basis with potentially dynamic hostnames. So having this function today is probably more motivated than back in 2016.
However, my scenario is just using keycloak to secure these review apps that appear on dynamic sites. If there is a different way to achieve it other than allowing wildcards in the hostname I could use that instead :-).

  Summary: [RFE] Authentication -> Flows table: Add the ability to edit flow post adding the flow
  Description: Currently it's not possible to edit (sub)flow name / label via the _Actions_ drop-down menu in the _Authentication_ -> _Flows_ table. Once the flow was added to the copy, the only way on how to change the subflow name is to delete it, and add it again with the proper / desired name. Since the subflow definition might contain advanced setup (might contain lot of executions), the need to edit subflow name / label better to reflect actual authentication flow, might be time consuming (the admin needs to delete the original flow, define a new one with desired name, then redefine all of the executions again).
Better approach IMHO would be, if the _Authentication_ -> _Flow_ table would offer _Edit flow_ action within the _Action_ drop-down menu.
*Note:* This RFE is *NOT* about the possibility to rename default flow names. Just about the ability to edit the derived ones, created by the user, from the default ones.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Improvements to re-authentication flows
  Description: In cases where the user is requested to re-authenticate the username is shown as an input field (some times empty I think). If the user enters a different username than the currently authenticated user an error message is displayed: "You are already authenticated as different user". This is not very good usability.
Examples of cases when a user can be requested to re-authenticate includes:
* login=prompt in an OIDC flow
* max_age in an OIDC flow
* An AIA is triggered, which requires re-auth
The proposed solution here is to display the details of the logged-in user with an option to restart the authentication process, similar to what we do on the OTP screen already:
 !screenshot-1.png|thumbnail! 
If a AIA is being triggered, the AIA should be cancelled (including kc_action_status=cancelled in the response to the app).
We also need to consider cases where password is not the first step that is presented to the user. Example of these include webauthn passwordless, identity broker, etc.. These should also have the "Not you" option, or in cases like the identity brokering most likely the correct solution is to simply destroy the session and create a new session if the user is changed.

  Summary: Using fine-grained admin permissions on groups, users should be able to create users without the role 'manage-users' according to the group permissions
  Description: Using fine-grained admin permissions on groups, a user in a group with *scope* permission 'manage' role should be able to create new users without the role 'manage-users'.
We have a scenario where we need to separate users in particular groups from each other. This works very well using fine-grained admin permissions with 'query-groups' and 'query-users' on realm-management client.
A local_admin_1 could only query users in group "users" and group "local admin", but could not see any super admin like "root admin".
However, the local_admin_1 could not create a user. If we add 'manager-users' to the group roles under realm-management client, all users are visible and no permissions are evaluated.
This is an essential use-case for our projects and is some-how related to #KEYCLOAK-7884
in one of the screenshots it can be seen that the option to create a new user is given, but once the dialog opens, the button "create" is not available.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn: polish after rebase
  Description: After rebase prototype with latest Keycloak master, WebAuthn was added to the prototype as it is already available in latest Keycloak master. We may have some remaining things to discuss & clarify. This JIRA is just to handle this possible remaining work around clarifying those points.
In case we agree that there is nothing more needed, we may just close the JIRA :)
The points were discussed on zulip (room #dev-auth and topic "multi-factor rebase"), so just copy/paste it here:
1) I've added the WebAuthnCredentialModel class (compatible with OTPCredentialModel and PasswordCredentialModel introduced in the prototype) and I've added fields 
"aaguid", "credentialId" and "counter" as part of CredentialData and "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" as part of SecretData. The only reason why I did is, 
that secretData are not displayed in the admin console. See screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-39-46.png
I am not sure if displaying "AttestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" won't make the data too big. But strictly said, WebAuthn credential doesn't have any confidential data. So should be "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" added to CredentialData too and displayed in the admin console? This will mean secretData will be just empty. WDYT?
2) The WebAuthn works in a bit different way than OTP. The WebAuthn authentication javascript call to "navigator.credentials.get" allows to pass more IDs of webAuthn credentials to the list of "allowed-credentials" and client itself can decide which credential he wants to use. So regarding this, I see few options:
a) The WebAuthnAuthenticator won't inherit from CredentialValidator interface. This means that in the Credentials selector list, which is described here there will be just single label "WebAuthn" . When this label is chosen, the checkbox is displayed when user can select the WebAuthn credentials, which he wants to use. This is the approach, which I used so far and you can see the screenshot how it looks like the screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-15-49.png
b) The WebAuthnAuthenticator will inherit from CredentialValidator interface. So Credentials selector list will contain separate items for each credential with labels like "WebAuthn - yubikey", "WebAuthn - chrome test" . There won't be checkbox selection on the page. So WebAuthn call to "navigator.credentials.get" will be always called just with single allowed credential.
c) Hybrid of 2 options above. There will be 2 labels and when particular label is chosen, the checkbox selection will be displayed as well on the WebAuthn page, but just with the single credential selected by default, which will correspond to the selected label. User has ability to select more credentials if he wants.
3) I removed the attributes from UserModel as I mentioned. Regarding the credentialId, I kept it just as single item in the WebAuthnCredentialData. In the keycloak master, you had it saved defacto 2 times:
a) the user attribute, which corresponds to the Base64URL encoded "rawId" returned from navigator.credentials.create
b) The attribute on the credential, which corresponds to the Base64 encoded of AttestedCredentialData.getCredentialId .
It seems to me from the WebAuthn specification and from my testing with yubikey and chrome testing api, that both those "credentialsId" are defacto same. So is it ok to save it just once in the credential model? In other words, the item returned from "rawId" is not saved.
